strengths: Provides an elegant, rigorous theoretical explanation for why paired sampling improves Shapley value estimation: the Shapley value depends only on the odd component of the value function, and paired sampling orthogonalizes regression into independent odd/even objectives (Theorem 3.2). This resolves an open conjecture posed by concurrent work (Fumagalli et al., 2026) and generalizes a prior result limited to degree-2 interactions (Mayer & Wuthrich, 2025).

The theoretical machinery is carefully built: equivalence of unanimity and Fourier bases on bounded-order collections (Lemma 3.4), consistency of Fourier regression (Theorem 3.5), and a clean derivation of exact efficiency constraints in the Fourier domain (Appendix C) are all proven with complete, checkable proofs.

The resulting algorithm, OddSHAP, is a practical and well-motivated consequence of the theory: it retains the consistency guarantee of polynomial regression methods while avoiding the O(d^2k) blow-up of PolySHAP by restricting to a sparse, proxy-selected odd-order Fourier subspace.

Extensive empirical evaluation across 8 diverse value functions (d=14 to 101, spanning vision, language, tabular, and synthetic domains) with multiple strong baselines (MSR, SVARM, Permutation Sampling, LeverageSHAP, RegressionMSR, PolySHAP) shows consistent state-of-the-art accuracy, with detailed ablations on evaluation cost, interaction count, and runtime component breakdown.

Code is provided, and the appendix contains thorough additional results (expanded tables with quartiles, runtime decomposition, simulated cost settings, interaction sparsity ablations) supporting reproducibility.
weaknesses: The core polynomial-regression consistency result (Theorem 2.2) and the paired-sampling conjecture being resolved are both drawn directly from a very recent, seemingly concurrent/unpublished work (Fumagalli et al., 2026, arXiv dated 2601), making the paper's novelty somewhat dependent on unverified concurrent results and reducing the extent to which the contribution can be judged as fully independent.

Comparison to PolySHAP, the most directly comparable method conceptually, is only feasible for 4 of the 8 lower-dimensional datasets ("3-PolySHAP") due to its scalability bottleneck, leaving the higher-dimensional regime (d=60-101) without a full apples-to-apples comparison against the closest baseline.

OddSHAP's runtime is shown to be comparable to or higher than several baselines (e.g., similar to RegressionMSR, higher than LeverageSHAP and MSR), so the practical efficiency gains are primarily relative to PolySHAP rather than an unambiguous overall runtime advantage; this nuance could be foregrounded more clearly in the main text rather than deferred to the appendix.

The method introduces several hyperparameters (η, GBT depth L, number of trees) whose sensitivity is only lightly explored (interaction-count ablation for η); a more systematic sensitivity analysis of the GBT proxy quality and its effect on final Shapley estimates is missing.

The Limitations section is brief and somewhat deferred to future work without deeper empirical investigation of failure cases (e.g., settings where odd/even components are highly correlated, as noted by Butler et al., which the paper acknowledges could hurt the odd-only approach but does not test).

strengths: The paper provides a genuine theoretical advance: it proves that the Shapley value depends exclusively on the odd component of the set function, and leverages this to give the first general proof that paired sampling orthogonally separates the regression objective into odd/even parts. This resolves an explicitly stated open conjecture from Fumagalli et al. (2026) about frontier invariance for general odd order k, which is a non-trivial and useful contribution to the theoretical understanding of a widely used heuristic.

The proposed OddSHAP algorithm is a natural and well-motivated consequence of the theory: by moving to the Fourier basis (where parity of interaction order corresponds exactly to odd/even class membership), the authors avoid the O(|T|^2 m) blow-up of full polynomial regression (PolySHAP) while retaining consistency guarantees, which prior sparse/proxy methods (FourierSHAP, ProxySPEX) lack.

The empirical evaluation is fairly extensive: 8 value functions spanning d=14 to d=101 across language, vision, tabular, and synthetic domains, with multiple sampling budgets, runtime-controlled comparisons (simulated evaluation costs from 0.001s to 1s), and ablations on the number of selected interactions and sample budget. OddSHAP achieves the best average rank across the main benchmark (Table 1) and is competitive or best across nearly all budget regimes in Figure 2.

Technical care is taken with implementation details that matter for fair comparison, e.g., exact (rather than soft, infinite-weight) enforcement of the efficiency boundary constraints via closed-form projection in the Fourier domain, and use of the same leverage-score sampling and LightGBM proxy configuration across baselines.

Proofs for the central claims (odd/even separation theorem, frontier invariance corollary, unanimity-Fourier basis equivalence, Fourier regression consistency) are included and appear complete and correct, lending credibility to the central narrative.
weaknesses: The foundational fact that the Shapley value depends only on the odd component follows quite directly from the symmetry p_{|S|-1} = p_{d-|S|} of the Shapley weighting kernel, and the paper's characterization of this as an 'elegant and fundamental' new insight may somewhat overstate its depth; the main novel technical content is really the paired-sampling orthogonalization theorem and its application, not the odd/even decomposition itself.

The practical algorithm is largely a recombination of existing components (paired sampling, Fourier/Mobius bases, ProxySPEX-style GBT interaction screening, constrained weighted least squares as in LeverageSHAP/PolySHAP), so the engineering novelty is incremental relative to very recent concurrent work (PolySHAP, RegressionMSR, ProxySPEX), several of which are 2025/2026 preprints, making it hard to assess how much of OddSHAP's advantage is attributable to the new theory versus implementation details (e.g., proxy hyperparameters, exact constraint handling already used by LeverageSHAP/PolySHAP).

Table 1 and the main figures omit PolySHAP results for the larger-d datasets (CG60, IL60, NHANES, Crime) entirely due to its scalability bottleneck, which is explained but still leaves an incomplete picture of how OddSHAP compares to the most expressive baseline in the regimes where interactions likely matter most.

The key hyperparameter η (controlling the size of the candidate interaction set relative to budget) is fixed at 10 throughout the main experiments with only a limited sensitivity ablation (Figure 4/11); the method's robustness to this choice across highly heterogeneous value functions (d=14 to d=101) is not deeply analyzed, and the paper shows that both too few and too many interactions can hurt performance, suggesting practical tuning may be needed.

In several benchmarks (e.g., DistilBERT, ViT16 in Table 1), the MSE improvement of OddSHAP over RegressionMSR is marginal or within likely noise bounds (same order of magnitude), undercutting the 'state-of-the-art' framing for lower-dimensional settings where the proposed method's main selling point (handling higher-order interactions efficiently) is less relevant.

No evaluation is provided on how estimation error translates into downstream utility (e.g., ranking consistency of feature importance, use in actual explanation-driven decisions), which would strengthen claims of practical significance beyond MSE on synthetic/benchmark ground truth.

The runtime analysis (Appendix D) shows OddSHAP's regression stage dominates and grows substantially with budget m, converging to runtimes similar to RegressionMSR and noticeably higher than LeverageSHAP; the 'efficiency' claim relative to the strongest simple baseline is therefore less clear-cut in wall-clock terms unless function evaluation cost dominates, which is not always the case in practice.

strengths: Provides a clean, well-proved theoretical insight (Shapley value depends only on the odd component of the value function) that yields the first general theoretical justification for the widely-used paired sampling heuristic, resolving an explicitly stated open conjecture from a concurrent/prior work (Fumagalli et al. 2026) and generalizing the degree-2 result of Mayer & Wuthrich.

The move from the unanimity basis to the Fourier basis is well-motivated and mathematically clean: Fourier terms decompose exactly into odd/even subspaces, which is the key structural property that makes restricting regression to odd-order terms both principled and tractable (Theorem 3.5, Lemma 3.4).

OddSHAP is a sensible and practical algorithm that combines a consistent regression guarantee (unlike pure proxy methods such as ProxySPEX/FourierSHAP) with the scalability benefits of proxy-guided interaction selection, directly addressing the quadratic blow-up of PolySHAP.

Extensive empirical evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks (language, vision, tabular, synthetic) spanning d=14 to d=101, with comparisons to a comprehensive set of strong baselines (MSR, SVARM, Permutation Sampling, LeverageSHAP, PolySHAP, RegressionMSR), consistently showing best or near-best average rank.

Useful ablations: cost-aware runtime simulation across several per-query cost regimes, decomposition of OddSHAP's runtime into components, and an ablation on number of selected odd interactions showing a clear and interpretable sparsity/overfitting trade-off.

Honest discussion of limitations, including the possibility that even/odd components may be correlated (per Butler et al. 2025) and that paired sampling may increase mutual coherence, suggesting concrete future directions.
weaknesses: The method is a fairly direct synthesis of several very recent/concurrent techniques (PolySHAP's polynomial regression consistency, ProxySPEX's GBT-based Fourier interaction screening, RegressionMSR's proxy+regression structure); the core algorithmic novelty beyond the odd/even theoretical insight is somewhat incremental, and the heavy reliance on near-simultaneous 2025/2026 preprints makes it hard to fully judge independent priority and benchmarking fairness.

3-PolySHAP, the most directly comparable consistent higher-order baseline, is missing from Table 1 and Figure 2 for four of the eight (largest) datasets, presumably due to computational infeasibility; this leaves the accuracy-vs-PolySHAP comparison incomplete exactly in the high-dimensional regime where OddSHAP's efficiency advantage is most claimed to matter.

The interaction screening step relies on an auxiliary GBT proxy (LightGBM, fixed depth=10) whose quality is not theoretically characterized; OddSHAP's accuracy inherits whatever bias/variance this proxy has in identifying true high-impact interactions, and sensitivity to proxy hyperparameters is only lightly explored.

Runtime analysis (Figure 6, Appendix D.1) shows that for large budgets the sparse regression step dominates OddSHAP's total runtime and scales similarly to RegressionMSR, suggesting that some of the claimed computational advantage over PolySHAP may erode as m grows, since |T| scales with m/η.

Possible evaluation circularity: for tabular datasets, both the ground-truth ϕ (via exact interventional TreeSHAP on an XGBoost model) and OddSHAP's/RegressionMSR's proxy (LightGBM GBT) are tree-based, which could structurally favor GBT-proxy methods relative to the deep-learning benchmarks; this potential confound is not discussed.

Only asymptotic consistency (m → 2^d) is established theoretically; no finite-sample error bounds or rate analysis are given to quantify how quickly OddSHAP/PolySHAP/Fourier-regression estimators converge relative to each other at practical budgets, leaving the strong empirical gains somewhat unexplained from a theoretical standpoint.

The key hyperparameter η controlling the size of the odd interaction support is fixed at 10 in the main experiments; while an ablation is provided in the appendix, no principled method for selecting η given a budget/dataset is proposed, leaving a practically important design choice largely heuristic.
